mainTopic: Vows between partners: the shared courtyard dispute and how big an owner's share (תפיסת יד) in a bathhouse must be to forbid it
overview: The amud continues the משנה about two partners in a courtyard who vowed not to benefit from each other. The חכמים forbid both of them to enter it, while רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says each one enters his own portion. One version of זעירי's teaching says the מחלוקת is only about a courtyard big enough to divide. רב יוסף challenges this from a בית הכנסת: it cannot be divided, yet a משנה forbids it. So he reverses the teaching: the מחלוקת is about a courtyard too small to divide, and in a large courtyard everyone forbids. רב הונא and רבי אלעזר both rule like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. Then the גמרא turns to the משנה about a friend's bathhouse and asks how big a share counts as תפיסת יד. רב נחמן says a half, a third or a quarter, while אביי says even less forbids, so it is permitted only when the owner takes a fixed rent (טסקא).

steps.title: First version: the dispute is only about a large courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רבה, quoting זעירי, says the מחלוקת is only about a courtyard big enough to divide. In a small courtyard everyone permits.
steps.simpleTranslation: The argument is about a courtyard that is big enough to split up. But if it is not big enough to split up, everyone agrees it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא hears a teaching that limits where the מחלוקת in the משנה applies. According to this version, the argument is only about a courtyard large enough to divide.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the courtyard is big enough to divide, each partner has a real piece the other could be forbidden to enter, so the חכמים forbid it. If it is too small to divide, the whole yard counts as belonging to both together, so this version says everyone permits it. This teaching starts in the text just before this section, where רבה quotes זעירי.

keyTerms.meaning: A dispute between opinions
Enough area to be divided between the partners
Everyone agrees
Permitted

phrases.english: The dispute is where the courtyard has enough to be divided.
But where it does not have enough to be divided,
everyone agrees it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines where the משנה's מחלוקת between the חכמים and רבי אליעזר בן יעקב applies.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מחלוקת applies only to a divisible courtyard; in an indivisible courtyard all agree it is permitted.

steps.title: Challenge from the synagogue
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף points out that a בית הכנסת cannot be divided, yet a משנה forbids it. That contradicts the idea that everyone permits an indivisible space.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said to him: Look at a synagogue. It is like something that cannot be divided. And yet we learned in a משנה: both of them are forbidden to use things that belong to that city!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף attacks the version from step 1. He uses a case where something cannot be divided and yet is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A בית הכנסת belongs to the whole town, and no one has his own piece of it, so it is like an indivisible courtyard. According to step 1, everyone should permit it. But a משנה says two people who vowed against each other are both forbidden to use town property like a בית הכנסת, so at least the חכמים forbid even an indivisible space.

keyTerms.meaning: Synagogue, which belongs to the whole town
Is similar to, is considered like
Property that belongs to the whole town

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is רבה, who quoted זעירי in the previous step.

phrases.english: Look at a synagogue,

phrases.aramaic: דִּכְמִי שֶׁאֵין בּוֹ כְּדֵי חֲלוּקָּה דָּמֵי,
phrases.english: which is like something that does not have enough to be divided,
and we learned in a mishna:

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנֵיהֶן אֲסוּרִין בְּדָבָר שֶׁל אוֹתָהּ הָעִיר!
phrases.english: Both of them are forbidden in something belonging to that city!
phrases.notes: This is a משנה from a little later in this פרק, about two people who vowed not to benefit from each other.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב יוֹסֵף: הֲרֵי בֵּית הַכְּנֶסֶת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the version of זעירי's teaching in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that everyone permits a space that cannot be divided.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A בית הכנסת is indivisible town property, yet a משנה forbids it to two people who vowed against each other. So an indivisible space is not permitted by everyone.

steps.title: Reversed version: the dispute is about a small courtyard
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף gives זעירי's teaching the other way around. The מחלוקת is about an indivisible courtyard, and in a divisible courtyard everyone forbids.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רב יוסף said that זעירי said: The argument is about a courtyard that is not big enough to split up. But if it is big enough to split up, everyone agrees it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the first version failed, רב יוסף says זעירי's teaching must be read the opposite way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the indivisible case is the one in dispute. The חכמים forbid it, which matches the בית הכנסת משנה. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב permits it, because each partner can say he is walking on his own share. In a divisible courtyard each partner has a defined piece, so entering it may mean stepping on the other's part, and everyone forbids it.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which signals that an earlier version is being replaced
Forbidden

steps.confusionAlert: Both versions are quotes of the same teaching of זעירי, and the two versions are exact opposites. רב יוסף is not just remembering it differently: because of his challenge from the בית הכנסת, he says זעירי must have said it the other way around. Keep track of which case is in dispute in each version.
steps.whyThisMatters: This version decides which courtyard case the מחלוקת, and later the הלכה, is talking about.

phrases.english: Rather, Rav Yosef said,
Ze'eiri said:
phrases.notes: רב יוסף is saying this must be what זעירי really said.

phrases.english: The dispute is where it does not have enough to be divided,
but where it has enough to be divided,
everyone agrees it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא, אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, אָמַר זְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2 by reversing the version of זעירי's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the teaching the opposite way
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The מחלוקת is about a divisible courtyard, and everyone permits an indivisible one.
steps.terutzMaskana: The מחלוקת is about an indivisible courtyard, where the חכמים forbid it, matching the בית הכנסת. In a divisible courtyard everyone forbids it.

steps.title: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and רבי אלעזר rules the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב. And רבי אלעזר also said: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the final ruling on the משנה's argument. Two אמוראים both rule like רבי אליעזר בן יעקב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case where the two sides disagree, the partners may each enter the courtyard and claim to be walking on their own share. The word 'וכן' shows that a second אמורא agrees, which makes the ruling stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: The practical law follows this opinion
And likewise, another authority agrees

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of זעירי's teaching. רב יוסף's version wins: the מחלוקת is about a courtyard too small to divide, and in a large courtyard everyone forbids. The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who lets each partner use his share.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.
And so too Rabbi Elazar said:
The halakha is in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer ben Ya'akov.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא: הֲלָכָה כְּרַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the case of the מחלוקת has been defined, gives the practical ruling.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, and two אמוראים, רב הונא and רבי אלעזר, agree on this.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about the friend's bathhouse
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the opening words of the משנה about a מודר הנאה whose friend owns a bathhouse in town.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: one who is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from his friend, and the friend has a bathhouse there, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting the משנה. This line sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה rules that the מודר may not use the friend's bathhouse if the friend still has תפיסת יד in it. The גמרא quotes only the first words and says וכו׳ ("etc.") to point us to the rest of that ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: A person forbidden by a vow from getting any benefit (from someone)
Bathhouse
"Etc.": the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: One who is forbidden by a vow from benefiting from his friend
and he (the friend) has a bathhouse there, etc.
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the משנה: if the owner still has a share (תפיסת יד) in it, the מודר may not use it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמּוּדָּר הֲנָאָה מֵחֲבֵירוֹ וְיֵשׁ לוֹ שָׁם מֶרְחָץ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic, separate from the courtyard discussion in steps 1-4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מודר may not use the friend's bathhouse if the owner keeps תפיסת יד in it.

steps.title: How big a share counts as תפיסת יד?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how much of a share in the profits counts as the owner's תפיסת יד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is 'a grip of the hand'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a definition: how big a share in the profits must the owner have before the bathhouse becomes forbidden to the מודר?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה used the term תפיסת יד but did not give a size. This is an honest question asking for a number. It is not an attack on the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'a grip of the hand': the owner still holding a share in the profits
And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is 'a grip of the hand'?
phrases.notes: He means: how big a share of the bathhouse income must the owner keep for it to count?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the definition of a term used in the משנה just quoted.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The minimum share of profits that counts as תפיסת יד.

steps.title: רב נחמן: only a half, a third, or a quarter
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן says תפיסת יד means the owner takes a half, a third, or a quarter of the profits. A smaller share does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: a half, a third, or a quarter. But with less, no.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers the question. A share of a half, a third, or a quarter is a real hold on the bathhouse, so it is forbidden. Anything smaller is not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רב נחמן, only a big share makes the bathhouse count as still the owner's, so that the מודר would be benefiting from him. A small share is not enough, so using the bathhouse is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: For a half, a third, or a quarter (of the income)
With less (a smaller share)

phrases.english: Rav Naḥman said:
For a half, a third, or a quarter.
phrases.notes: These are the common deals where the owner takes that fraction of what the bathhouse earns.

phrases.english: But with less, no.
phrases.notes: "No" means it does not count as תפיסת יד, so the מודר may use the bathhouse.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לְמֶחֱצָה לִשְׁלִישׁ וְלִרְבִיעַ
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A share of a half, a third, or a quarter counts as תפיסת יד. A smaller share does not.

steps.title: אביי: even a smaller share forbids
steps.stepSummary: אביי disagrees with רב נחמן. Even a share smaller than a quarter forbids the bathhouse to the מודר.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: even with less, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי gives a different answer to the same question. Any share in the profits, even a small one, makes the bathhouse forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For אביי, size does not matter. As long as the owner earns anything based on how the bathhouse is used, the מודר's use helps the owner, so it is forbidden.

keyTerms.meaning: Even
Forbidden

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Even with less, it is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with רב נחמן's answer in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Any share in the profits, even less than a quarter, counts as תפיסת יד.

steps.title: When is it permitted? Only with a fixed rent
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains אביי's view. The only permitted case is when the owner receives a fixed rent (טסקא) and has no share in the profits.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case where it is permitted? Where he receives a fixed rent.
steps.whatsHappening: Since אביי forbids even a tiny share, the גמרא asks when the bathhouse could ever be permitted. The answer: when the owner just collects a set rent.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a fixed rent, the owner gets the same money no matter how many people use the bathhouse. So the מודר's bathing gives the owner nothing, and he has no תפיסת יד at all.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? How does it look?
That it is permitted
A fixed rent payment, not tied to the profits

steps.whatToRemember: רב נחמן: only a half, a third, or a quarter counts as תפיסת יד. אביי: any share forbids, and the bathhouse is permitted only when the owner gets a fixed rent (טסקא).

phrases.english: What is the case where it is permitted?
Where he receives a fixed rent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains what case is left permitted under אביי's strict view in step 8.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: It is permitted only when the owner receives a fixed rent (טסקא).
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: For אביי, the bathhouse is permitted only when the owner's income is a fixed rent.
